To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NMDA receptor subunit expression varies according to regional vulnerability to pathological damage in Alzheimer's disease.
the expression of the NMDAr modulatory NR2A and B isoforms is decreased in susceptible regions of Alzheimer's disease brain.
the expression of NR2 subunits varies in different regions of the brain and that the levels are altered in AD brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the glutamatergic neurotransmitter system in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (for review see Coyle, 1997; Coyle and Kershaw, 1997).
the expression of the NMDAR1 subunit mRNA in the human brain and in Alzheimer's disease, and with the role of the NMDAr1 subunit in neuronal death and neuroprotection in Alzheimer's disease.
the molecular mechanisms that lead to neuronal loss in Alzheimer's disease and the role of NMDA receptors in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NMDA receptors are involved in the pathogenesis of AD and that the NMDA receptors play an important role in the selective vulnerability of certain neuronal populations in AD.
NMDA receptor subunits are down‐regulated in AD brain, but that the degree and the extent of the down‐regulation varies with the different subunits.
the NR1 subunit splice variant expression pattern in the AD hippocampus is different from that of the controls.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in AD brain, the NR1 splice variants and the NR2A, B subunits are downregulated in susceptible regions, whereas the NR2C and D subunits are not affected.
the NMDA receptors in Alzheimer's disease brain have altered subunit composition.
NMDA receptor subunit composition may contribute to the selective vulnerability of neurons to excitotoxicity in AD brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NMDA receptors in AD are differentially regulated in a region‐specific manner.
the NMDAR NR2 subunit isoforms have a differential expression in AD brain.
there is a differential expression of the different NMDA receptor subunits in Alzheimer disease.
